newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to keep 1997 budget within plan - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Poland to keep 1997 budget within plan - analyst.

text.p: A senior economist said on Friday Poland should meet this year's budget gap target of 2.8 percent of GDP and without amending the budget to cover damage of this week's flooding.

Andrzej Wernik, head of the state-funded, semi-independent Institute of Finance, told Reuters in an interview possible costs of relief operations should not reach levels that would require changing the budget.

"The sums that could be needed are relatively small, some of the financing would come from outside of the budget and the budget law allows enough flexibility to make necessary adjustments," Wernik said.

He said that the overall budget situation should be improving in the second half of the year largely thanks to seasonal factors such as a usual pickup in business activity and higher revenues from excise or value added taxes.
"On the revenue side the inflows from personal income taxes will be definitely lower than planned...but other revenues, mainly from indirect taxes, should be higher," Wernik said.
Income tax revenues in the first five months of the year fell below plan as the finance ministry underestimated the scope of tax refunds claimed by individuals which put the budget under pressure.
But Wernik said the second half of the year was always better for the budget as the end of tax the refunds period and the move of taxpayers to higher tax brackets eased pressure on debt financing.

"There are ongoing problems with financing the deficit on the domestic market...but unless there is a sudden worsening of the economic climate the situation in the second half should improve," he said.

After the first five months of 1997, Poland's budget gap reached 53.8 percent of the 12.22 billion zloty shortfall planned for the whole year and the Finance Ministry is due to release official data for the first half next week.
Budget revenues in the January-May period amounted to 35.3 percent of this year's plan while spending in the same period reached 37.1 percent
